summary: Review firewater, foam and water-spray decisions for oil and gas facilities. Explore the course outline and practical design-review outcomes.
lede: Fire protection system design review connects credible fire scenarios with safeguards suited to facility exposure and firewater constraints. For fire protection, process safety and project engineers, and oil and gas HSE managers, the course builds practical review skills for assessing firewater capacity, comparing water-spray and foam options, and marking up design documents. It also covers detection and alarm interfaces, impairment readiness, and prioritizing findings for project and operations decisions.
audienceIntro: This course suits technical professionals who select, review or maintain fire-protection systems for oil and gas facilities. It is designed for people who need to connect fire scenarios and facility drawings to practical design and operating decisions.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of oil and gas process equipment, facility layouts and basic fire-safety terminology; no programming is required.
